meta.description: Plan your visit to BIFF Square (BIFF광장) in Busan: street food, how to get there from Jagalchi Station, opening hours, the Star Road handprints and nearby Gukje Market. A complete non-profit visitor guide.

nonprofitBanner.text: This is an independent, non-profit guide compiled by travel enthusiasts to provide the most objective information about visiting BIFF Square. It is free, and we are affiliated with no organization.
nonprofitBanner.dataSource: All attraction information on this site is cross-checked against public materials from the Korea Tourism Organization (VisitKorea), the Busan Metropolitan City and Jung-gu District Office, with no commercial recommendations.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.text: So that every traveler coming to Busan can experience this street corner that gave birth to the Busan International Film Festival, we have organized scattered official information into this guide — only to give you the purest film culture, Star Road and urban stroll.

hero.title: BIFF Square (BIFF광장)
hero.subtitle: A cinematic urban landmark in Nampo-dong, Jung-gu, Busan. The Busan International Film Festival was founded here in 1996, and the square was redeveloped and renamed BIFF Square in 2011 as the festival's acronym changed. It is paved with the handprints and footprints of over a hundred film directors and actors (Star Road), and since the festival's main venue moved to Haeundae in 2011, it has become the festival's birthplace and the core stage of 'Community BIFF (community film festival)', as well as a beloved street-food spot (seed/nut sugar pancake, Ssiat Hotteok) — one of Korea's most representative film-themed street landmarks.

sunsetPlanner.title: Based on today's sunset, we suggest arriving about 60 minutes earlier to catch both the softest diffuse light and the blue-hour sky — ideal for photographing the Star Road handprints and the Nampo-dong streetscape.
sunsetPlanner.note: The square is surrounded by tall buildings and neon; light is warmest from afternoon to dusk. On festival weekends (October) or holidays, allow extra time to avoid the crowds.
sunsetPlanner.seaGlare: Night-light note: BIFF Square sits at the commercial heart of Nampo-dong. After dark, neon and shop lights are dense, making it a golden window for cinematic street shots and portraits; for handheld night photography, raise the ISO or use stabilization.

quickFactsDashboard.title: BIFF Square at a Glance · Data Board
quickFactsDashboard.subtitle: A few numbers to understand this street corner that gave birth to the Busan International Film Festival.

items.label: Founded / Founded
items.note: The Busan International Film Festival (then PIFF) was founded in 1996; the BIFF Square area has since become one of the birthplaces of Korean film culture.

items.label: Star Road / Star Road
items.note: The square is paved with the handprints and footprints of hundreds of directors and actors — Korea's most recognizable Star Road of filmmakers.

items.label: Festival / Festival
items.note: The Busan International Film Festival is one of Asia's most influential film festivals; BIFF Square is the festival's birthplace and the core stage of 'Community BIFF', while the grand opening/closing carpet moved to the Busan Cinema Center in Haeundae in 2011.

items.label: Role / Role
items.note: Since the main venue moved to Haeundae in 2011, the square keeps Star Road and became a community-film-festival stage — free, open and full of everyday bustle, a civic living room where film meets the street.

items.label: Location / Location
items.note: Plus Code: 32XH+7M Busan. At 58-1 Gudeok-ro, Nampo-dong, Jung-gu, Busan, next to Gukje Market and Bosudong Bookstore Street.

items.label: Nearby / Nearby
items.note: Organically linked with Nampo-dong, Gukje Market, Bosudong Bookstore Street and the 40 Steps — the starting point for Busan's modern history and culture trail.

hiddenRules.title: Tips for Visiting the City Square
hiddenRules.subtitle: BIFF Square is an open street landmark at the commercial heart of Nampo-dong. Think through safety, timing and budget, and the experience upgrades from 'rushing check-ins' to 'relaxed, safe play'.

highlights.label: Secure belongings
highlights.note: The square and surrounding district are crowded; pickpocket risk is relatively high. Keep phones and wallets in front pockets, wear bags in front, and stay alert at night.

highlights.label: Festival control
highlights.note: During the October festival, the square and surrounding roads often see temporary traffic control and crowd management. Follow on-site guidance and allow extra time.

highlights.label: Weather & routine
highlights.note: Busan is hot and rainy in summer with limited shade at the square; carry rain gear and drinking water, and protect against sun and heat at midday.

panels.q: Is there an admission fee for BIFF Square?
panels.a: BIFF Square is an open public space, free all year and accessible 24 hours with no gate and no reservation — visit anytime (keep quiet at night and respect local residents).
items: The public square area is open 24 hours, anytime.
The Star Road handprints are freely viewable all day.

panels.q: What is different during the festival?
panels.a: Every October during the Busan International Film Festival, the grand opening/closing carpet and awards moved to the Busan Cinema Center in Haeundae's Centum City; BIFF Square, as the festival's birthplace, hosts 'Community BIFF' open-air screenings, star handprint unveilings and fan markets, with crowd control and some surrounding roads closing temporarily. If you come specifically for the carpet, head to Haeundae and check the day's schedule in advance.
items: Grand carpet & awards: Busan Cinema Center, Haeundae (since 2011).
BIFF Square: Community BIFF screenings, handprint unveilings & fan markets; crowds and closures are heavier in festival time — prefer public transit.

panels.q: Is it convenient with children or seniors?
panels.a: The square lies in the flat Nampo-dong commercial area, generally level and accessibility-friendly, suitable for families and slow strolls with seniors; but holidays and the festival get crowded — avoid peaks, hold children's hands and mind your belongings.

complianceGuide.title: BIFF Square · Visitor Etiquette & Public Environment Guide
complianceGuide.subtitle: This is both visitors' film landmark and a street Busan citizens walk through daily. Following these rules is respect for film culture and for others.

rules.title: Take your trash with you
rules.text: The square is in a commercial district with limited bins. Bring a small bag and take everything away, especially cigarette butts, plastics and food waste, keeping the corner tidy.

rules.title: Quiet remembrance & courtesy
rules.text: Star Road carries the shared memory of filmmakers and fans. Lower your voice and don't blast music, leaving the space for those taking photos and pausing.

rules.title: Mind no-smoking & fire rules
rules.text: Some arcades and neighboring buildings are no-smoking zones. Follow on-site no-smoking and fire signs; do not smoke among wooden fixtures or crowds.

rules.title: Respect film culture
rules.text: Handprint and footprint plates and the red-carpet marker are memorial public art. Do not step on, carve or misbehave on them; keep the film-culture space solemn and alive.

higashiyamaRoute.title: Half-Day Route · Closed Loop
higashiyamaRoute.subtitle: Not just 'who it suits', but a strongly logical closed loop you can follow directly: from filmmakers' handprints, to the landmark arch, then to street food and the old-book street — a complete 'film + everyday' package in half a day.

steps.title: Star Road & directors' handprints
steps.text: From Jagalchi Station (Busan Line 1), Exit 7, it's about a 3–5 min walk to the main entrance (Nampo Station, Exit 7 is about a 5 min walk as an alternative). In the soft morning or dusk light look for the handprint plates of international auteurs such as Hou Hsiao-hsien, Akira Kurosawa and Takeshi Kitano.
tips: Star Road is open and level; morning and dusk light are best with fewer crowds.
The handprint plates are embedded in the pavement; crouch low for better composition.

steps.title: Photo stop: BIFF landmark arch
steps.text: Take photos under the giant yellow semi-circular arch on the south side of the square, capturing the most Busan-film-street landmark view, framed together with the Star Road handprints.
tips: The arch is the square's most photogenic spot; queue courteously.
For backlit shots, leave negative space with the arch silhouette.

steps.title: Taste break: seed pancake & fish cake
steps.text: In front of the dense red-and-yellow umbrella stalls at the center of the square, queue for a freshly fried 'seed/nut sugar pancake (Ssiat Hotteok)' — crisp outside, filled with sunflower and pumpkin seeds; pair it with a skewer of hot fish cake (Eomuk) for the authentic BIFF flavor.
tips: Eat the seed pancake while hot; the filling can be scalding.
The red-and-yellow umbrella stalls are an iconic image of Nampo-dong street food.

steps.title: Cultural extension: market & bookstreet
steps.text: Head north across the main road into Gukje Market, then walk on to Bosudong Bookstore Street to explore the used-book and craft culture that has survived since the Korean War, collecting film narrative and urban memory together.
tips: Market food is dense; graze lightly across many stalls.
Bosudong Bookstreet's old books and film cameras are popular themes — best browsed slowly.

higashiyamaRoute.disclaimer: The route emphasizes a closed loop that 'works even if you just follow it'; if short on time, keep the first two segments as the core, and treat the food and bookstreet as flexible add-ons.

intro.title: Getting to Know BIFF Square
intro.description: BIFF Square (BIFF광장) lies at 58-1 Gudeok-ro, Nampo-dong, Jung-gu, Busan, next to Gukje Market and Bosudong Bookstore Street — an urban film-culture landmark that gave birth to the Busan International Film Festival. The Busan International Film Festival (then PIFF) was founded here in 1996, and in 2011, as the festival's acronym changed from PIFF to BIFF, the square was redeveloped and renamed BIFF Square. It is paved with the handprints and footprints of over a hundred film directors and actors (Star Road); it is the birthplace of the festival and the core stage of 'Community BIFF (community film festival)', as well as a beloved street-food spot (seed/nut sugar pancake, Ssiat Hotteok) — one of Korea's most representative film-themed street landmarks.

visitGuide.title: Visit Guide
visitGuide.description: BIFF Square is a free, open public space with no gate and no reservation; the square area is accessible 24 hours. The ideal approach is usually not 'wander by day' but reverse-planning around light: come at dawn or dusk for the best light on Star Road, and prefer weekdays for quiet photos. Facilities are restrained and commercial feel is low — which is exactly its charm.
items: Best at dawn or dusk: Nampo-dong light is softest then, and handprints with the carpet frame best.
Best viewpoints are the middle of Star Road and the BIFF marker wall.
About a 3–5 min walk from Jagalchi Station (Busan Line 1), Exit 7, to the square (Nampo Station, Exit 7 is about a 5 min walk as an alternative).
Almost no commercial supply at the square; water, restrooms and breaks are better in the surrounding district.

alsoKnownAs.title: Highlights
items: Star Road of handprints and footprints from over a hundred filmmakers — Korea's most recognizable film landmark
Birthplace of the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) and core stage of 'Community BIFF', a community film carnival every October
A beloved street-food spot: the signature 'seed/nut sugar pancake (Ssiat Hotteok)' is crisp outside and filled with sunflower and pumpkin seeds
Next to Gukje Market and Bosudong Bookstore Street, where film culture meets everyday bustle
Linked with the 40 Steps and Yongdusan Park, forming Busan's modern history and culture trail
Free, open public space accessible 24 hours — stroll and snap anytime

transportSection.title: Transportation & Getting Here
transportSection.subtitle: Combine arriving in Busan, city transfers, walking/cycling, parking and charging into one clear structure for planning your BIFF Square trip.
transportSection.overviewText: BIFF Square is at 58-1 Gudeok-ro, Nampo-dong, Jung-gu, Busan, next to Gukje Market and Bosudong Bookstore Street — a representative film-culture landmark of Busan. The easiest long-distance option is KTX from Seoul to Busan Station, about 2.5 hours; once in the city, the closest subway is Jagalchi Station (Busan Line 1), Exit 7, about a 3–5 min walk. Nampo Station (Line 1), Exit 7 is also about a 5 min walk and works as an alternative approach.
transportSection.overviewText2: BIFF Square is an open street corner with no gate. Plan transport, parking and walking together — especially with seniors, children or luggage, parking at a public lot then walking in saves a lot of hassle.
arrivalItems: BIFF Square is in Nampo-dong; the closest subway is Jagalchi Station (Busan Line 1), Exit 7, about a 3–5 min walk. Nampo Station (Line 1), Exit 7 is about a 5 min walk as an alternative.
Several public parking lots surround the square; they fill fast on peak weekends — arrive early or prefer transit.
Crowds are higher during the festival (October); strongly prefer public transit or off-peak visits.

parking.title: Parking & Charging Overview
parking.note: Several public and mall parking lots surround BIFF Square; below are the nearest main options. Rates and availability vary by season and time — follow on-site signs.

options.name: Gukje Market parking tower
options.price: Mall / paid, more spaces but tight in peak

options.name: Surrounding street parking
options.price: Roadside / small lots, few spaces, easier off-peak

options.name: Yongdusan Park parking
options.price: Attraction annex parking, tight on holidays

parking.disclaimer: Square roads are extremely congested on holidays and festival time; do not block bus and fire lanes. EV chargers are common at Nampo-dong malls and public lots; rates and limits may change — check posted signs.

driverFaq.q: Is there parking near BIFF Square?
driverFaq.a: Several public and mall lots surround the square, such as Nampo-dong public parking and the Gukje Market parking tower, within walking distance. They fill fast on peak weekends — arrive early or prefer transit.
Nampo-dong public parking is about 100–300 m away, the closest to the square; the Gukje Market parking tower is about 200–500 m, more spaces but tight in peak.
Very little. Square roads are narrow and congested on holidays; use proper lots and public transit, no long roadside parking.

driverFaq.q: Is driving recommended for BIFF Square?
driverFaq.a: Unless parking is essential, driving is not advised. Weekends and festival time are very congested; walking or transit is smoother. If driving, park at a surrounding lot then walk in.

Strongly. Take Busan Line 1 to Jagalchi Station, Exit 7, then walk about 3–5 min to the square (Nampo Station, Exit 7 is about a 5 min walk as an alternative). Address: 58-1 Gudeok-ro, Jung-gu, Busan, South Korea.

driverFaq.q: What is the best way to get here?
driverFaq.a: For stability and ease, transit is still best: Busan Line 1 to Jagalchi Station, Exit 7, walk in. If you must drive, treat parking and transfer as part of the trip, not 'park at the door'.

localTips: Dawn and dusk remain the golden windows, but set your baseline as 'arrive 60 min before sunset' — best for Star Road handprints and the carpet.
Crowds are high on weekends and during the festival; allow buffer and off-peak time with kids or gear.
BIFF Square pairs best with Gukje Market, Bosudong Bookstreet and Yongdusan Park; a single stop underestimates its cultural value.

bestTime.title: Best time to arrive
bestTime.text: BIFF Square is accessible all day, but the photo ceiling is the dawn and dusk light window. Arrive about 60 min before sunset; if weather is poor for photos, shift focus to Gukje Market food, Bosudong Bookstreet or the Yongdusan Park night view.

officialManagement.title: Landmark Archive
officialManagement.text: It is the cradle of Asia's new-wave cinema and Busan's most locally warm civic living room. Here, the handprint plates of international masters lie right beside the griddle of street-food stalls — high art and everyday bustle have never been so naturally reconciled.

timeline.title: History · Three-Act Timeline
timeline.subtitle: Place the prehistory, renaming and main-venue move of the Busan International Film Festival on one axis to truly understand why this corner is more than 'a pretty square'.

items.title: PIFF era begins
items.text: In 1996 the first Busan International Film Festival (then PIFF, Pusan International Film Festival) opened here, and the Nampo-dong street corner became the celebration stage for Asian filmmakers, laying Busan's city identity as a 'city of film'.

items.title: Renaming & venue move
items.text: In 2011 the acronym was officially changed from PIFF to BIFF. The same year, the festival's main venue, carpet ceremony and closing moved to the Busan Cinema Center in Haeundae's Centum City, while BIFF Square kept Star Road and was modernized.

items.title: Community BIFF era
items.text: From 2018 to now, the 'Community BIFF (community film festival)' section was introduced; screening rights returned to the Nampo-dong neighborhood, with open-air screenings, handprint unveilings and fan markets bringing film art fully into the street corner.

humanities.title: Humanities & Film Theme Research
humanities.subtitle: Put the prehistory of the Busan International Film Festival, the square's renaming, and the memory of Star Road and the red carpet on one timeline to truly understand why this corner is more than 'a pretty square'.

sections.title: Founding intent: born for Asian cinema
sections.content: In 1996, the Busan International Film Festival (then PIFF, Pusan International Film Festival) was founded in Busan — Korea's first international film event. The BIFF Square area has since become the core stage for the festival's opening/closing and fan gatherings, anchoring Busan's city positioning as the 'city of film'.

sections.title: The name 'BIFF': from PIFF to BIFF
sections.content: In 2011, the Busan International Film Festival changed its acronym from PIFF to BIFF (Busan International Film Festival), and the square was redeveloped and officially renamed 'BIFF Square' that same year. The same year, the festival's main venue, carpet ceremony and closing moved to the Busan Cinema Center (Busan Cinema Center) in Haeundae's Centum City. The name hides both the festival's growth story and Busan's cultural ambition toward the world.

sections.title: Star Road: filmmakers' handprint plates
sections.content: The square is paved with the handprints and footprints of over a hundred film directors and actors, forming the famous 'Star Road'. From international auteurs to Korean stars, their traces are permanently embedded in the pavement, letting ordinary visitors 'shake hands' with film history.

sections.title: From red carpet to community film festival
sections.content: Since 2011, the festival's grand opening/closing carpet and awards have moved to the Busan Cinema Center in Haeundae; BIFF Square keeps Star Road, star handprint unveilings and fan markets, transforming into the festival's 'spiritual birthplace' and the core stage of 'Community BIFF'. On ordinary days it is one of Korea's most cinematic — and most human — street scenes.

sections.title: Symbiosis with Gukje Market
sections.content: BIFF Square is next to Busan's famous Gukje Market (국제시장). Film culture and everyday bustle meet here. After Star Road, turn around and dive into the market's rice cakes, fish cakes and old Busan flavors — a unique 'film + life' experience.

sections.title: Bosudong Bookstreet & the 40 Steps
sections.content: A short walk from the square is Bosudong Bookstore Street — a literary district known for used books and crafts — and the 40 Steps (40계단), which witness the civilian migration history around the Korean War. Together with BIFF Square they string together Busan's modern history and cultural fabric.

sections.title: BIFF's standing in Asian cinema
sections.content: The Busan International Film Festival is one of Asia's most influential film festivals, with the spirit of 'Today's cinema, tomorrow's Asia', long supporting emerging directors and Asian cinema. As its core landmark, BIFF Square is the concrete starting point of this urban film ambition.

didYouKnow.title: Did you know?
didYouKnow.text: BIFF Square is not just a square but a street museum of Korean film culture — from the festival's 1996 founding, through the 2011 redevelopment and renaming, to the handprints of over a hundred filmmakers on Star Road, land and film memory are written into the same Nampo-dong corner.

sitePlaques.title: Reading the On-Site Signs
sitePlaques.subtitle: What's worth reading slowly on site is often not the photo badge, but the official signs explaining 'why this corner is here'.
sitePlaques.intro: The readings below are based on BIFF Square introductions, Star Road notes and festival guides set by Busan Metropolitan City and Jung-gu District Office, turning information visible on site but not always read closely into understandable English.

items.title: BIFF Square & the festival
items.body: These signs give the key background: the 1996 founding of the Busan International Film Festival (PIFF), and the meaning of the 2011 redevelopment and renaming to BIFF Square. Reading the signs is lesson one in using this film landmark.

items.title: Handprint plates & Star Road
items.body: The signs stress BIFF Square's status as a film-culture landmark and remind visitors that half the charm is the filmmakers' handprints, half is the real film history underfoot. They explain clearly 'why so many handprints'.

items.title: Spiritual birthplace · Community BIFF
items.body: The guide explains 'why this is the spiritual birthplace of the festival'. Although the grand opening/closing carpet moved to the Busan Cinema Center in Haeundae in 2011, every October star handprint unveilings and 'Community BIFF' open-air screenings are still held here; seeing it with Star Road, BIFF Square's design logic becomes clear: film glory and civic life coexist.

items.title: Where film meets the street
items.body: Erected by Jung-gu District Office, marking the link between BIFF Square and the adjacent Gukje Market. It reminds every visitor: this corner connects Busan's most fiery old commercial district with its most dazzling film culture.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Practical information about BIFF Square's facilities, history and visit planning.

items.label: Parking
items.value: Nampo-dong public lot / Gukje Market tower

items.q: Is there parking, and what does it cost?
items.a: Several public and mall lots surround the square, such as Nampo-dong public parking and the Gukje Market tower, within walking distance. Mostly paid; they fill fast on peak weekends — arrive early or prefer transit.

Nampo-dong and BIFF Square are flat with accessible ramps; wheelchairs and strollers can reach Star Road and the carpet area fairly easily. Crowds are heavy on holidays — stay on hard surfaces and bring company.

items.q: Are there restrooms or food on site?
items.a: The square itself is an open corner; restrooms and food concentrate in the surrounding Nampo-dong district and Gukje Market. Stock up on water and food in the district before entering.

items.q: Is there a gas station or EV charging nearby?
items.a: EV chargers are at Nampo-dong malls and public lots; conventional gas stations line Busan Station and the city, handy for drivers to refuel on the way in.

items.q: What does 'BIFF Square' have to do with film?
items.a: 'BIFF' comes from the Busan International Film Festival's acronym. The square was redeveloped and renamed BIFF Square in 2011 as the festival changed from PIFF to BIFF — an important Korean film-culture landmark. The name hides both the festival's growth story and Busan's cultural ambition toward the world.

items.q: What is its special natural and human value?
items.a: BIFF Square is not a themed park, but a street corner where citizens turned a Nampo-dong block into a cultural landmark holding together film glory, fan memory, handprint art and everyday bustle. Star Road, the carpet and the surrounding market form a low-impact, high-empathy design and one of Busan's 'film and harbor' city cards.
BIFF Square is an open public space, free long-term, accessible 24 hours, no gate, no ticket or reservation — visit anytime (respect film culture, avoid late-night noise).

items.q: How long does a visit take?
items.a: A relaxed visit is about 1–2 hours (including Star Road and photo stops); if you add Gukje Market, Bosudong Bookstreet or Yongdusan Park, reserve a half day.

items.q: Can I still go in bad weather?
items.a: Yes — it is an open corner, accessible in any weather. But during typhoons, heavy rain or thunderstorms mind wind and lightning; wear non-slip shoes and watch weather; the handprint plates are slippery when wet.

items.q: What else is worth visiting nearby?
items.a: From BIFF Square you can link Gukje Market (국제시장), Bosudong Bookstore Street (보수동 책방골목), the 40 Steps (40계단), Yongdusan Park (용두산공원) and Busan Tower, forming a 'handprints – carpet – market – harbor' half-day culture route.

scienceArt.title: Film & City: Handprints, Carpet and Harbor
scienceArt.subtitle: Dig one layer below the surface 'good looks' to find what is truly rare here: it is at once a film landmark, a piece of urban memory, and an open-air film-culture classroom.

scienceMuseum.name: Busan International Film Festival & BIFF Square
scienceMuseum.role: A film landmark built into the district
scienceMuseum.highlight: The hardest part of BIFF Square is both visible and invisible. Visible are the handprint plates and the carpet; invisible is the Busan film ambition and the growth history of Asian emerging cinema it carries. Visitors see a streetscape; fans see a memory system still running.
points: Core: film glory, fan memory and urban geography light up this corner.
Key: public space transformed into a low-impact, high-empathy film classroom.
Meaning: it upgrades 'district corner' into a publicly pilgrimage-worthy film model.

artMuseum.name: The film symbols in Star Road
artMuseum.highlight: The handprint plates, the carpet and the Nampo-dong neon, together with Busan harbor, form BIFF Square's identity system: instantly readable as belonging to Busan, to film, and to a gentle, vivid film aesthetics. From film glory to everyday bustle, this contrast makes it one of Busan's most memorable cultural images.
points: Imagery: handprints, carpet, neon form strong recognition.
Status: Busan's most photogenic film landmark.
Narrative: it translates the film theme into a publicly felt aesthetic experience.

outdoorMuseum.title: Photo & Spotting Guide: BIFF Square's Photo Spots
outdoorMuseum.subtitle: As Busan's most recognizable film landmark, a few structured spots and times greatly improve your photos' usefulness and beauty.

items.name: Star Road · handprint galaxy
items.background: From dawn to dusk, the handprint plates of over a hundred filmmakers spread across the pavement — BIFF Square's classic 'handprint – corner' composition, with handprint silhouettes especially moving in backlight.
points: Use the handprint plates as a lead-in to the horizon.
Crouch low to layer handprints and pavement for a steadier frame.

items.name: Red-carpet area · film overlook
items.background: Shoot the carpet area from below or from the square to frame 'carpet + corner + Nampo-dong' together — BIFF Square's most recognizable spot.
points: Side-light at dawn makes the carpet marker softest.
Mind your feet and crowds; don't enter closed zones for a frame.

items.name: BIFF marker wall & dusk
items.background: Blue hour (20–30 min after sunset) balances sky and pavement best — the strongest mood window, the marker wall striking against the cool sky.
points: Shoot at blue hour for the most balanced sky and pavement.
Silhouette the marker wall leaving a large warm corner.

items.name: Nampo-dong night lights
items.background: At night the Nampo-dong neon lights up and BIFF Square mirrors a river of lights — good for a closing long-exposure night shot and portraits.
points: Use the neon streetscape as a lead-in to the distance.
Raise ISO or use stabilization for night shots.

education.title: Why is this Busan's film landmark?
education.subtitle: What's most worth learning about BIFF Square is not 'it got pretty', but how a Nampo-dong corner was brought back into public film memory while keeping reverence for culture.

points.title: A film living room still used by citizens
points.text: BIFF Square is not a 'hide the film and done' case, but a sample that continuously activates the film landmark through public-space design and turns it into a shared place.
items: Citizens entrust daily walks and fan pilgrimages to this corner.
Public space and city life coexist long-term.

points.title: Writing film ethics into visitor behavior
points.text: The signs, handprint plates and guide system are not just guides, but let every visitor, while using the space, take part in respect for film culture and others.
items: Visitors are guided to stay on low-impact paths.
Pilgrimage experience and public life are not sacrificed to each other.

points.title: Turning film memory into public aesthetics
points.text: BIFF Square did not erase the film prehistory, but through handprints, the carpet and signs lets the public, while visiting, realize what this land has gone through.
items: Story depth and pilgrimage experience complete at the same place.
This is exactly the value a non-profit science site should amplify.

items.tip: Save energy for the photo stops rather than spending it on crowds.

items.resonance: Dawn and dusk handprint galaxy are Busan's most romantic frames, very photogenic.

items.resonance: As a film-landmark sample, the festival prehistory, carpet and handprints are worth a close look.
items.tip: Avoid the most crowded weekends; choose dawn or weekday afternoons to truly observe details.

items.resonance: Without going far to the countryside, you can observe Korean film culture, everyday bustle and harbor geography in central Busan, and link subway, bus and local food — an ideal starting point to understand Busan's 'film and harbor' character.
items.tip: If you can only pick one Busan landmark, BIFF Square is the best first stop for the 'film and city' theme.

lodging.title: Lodging Guide: Stay close, or stay convenient
lodging.subtitle: Busan is a port city where 'mountain-sea and city connect'. We don't recommend specific hotels, but help you analyze two lodging patterns to choose what suits you.

options.name: Nampo-dong / Jung-gu area
options.highlight: Staying in Nampo-dong or Jung-gu, you walk or take a short ride to BIFF Square, Gukje Market and Bosudong Bookstreet; the night neon and sea breeze suit travelers. Best for those focused on 'film stroll + shopping' with high convenience needs.
options.commute: Commute: about 5–15 min walk to the square, about 5–10 min to Gukje Market. Low demand on legs, good for early-morning square walks.
points: About 5–15 min walk to Star Road, least effort.
Very rich district night views and dining.
More choices, usually better value.

options.name: Seomyeon / Haeundae area
options.highlight: Staying in Seomyeon or Haeundae, next to subway hubs, beaches and food streets, best for those focused on 'beach + transfer', then take subway to BIFF Square by day.
options.commute: Commute: about 20–40 min by subway to Nampo Station. Good for drivers or independent travelers wanting absolute convenience.
points: Subway hub and beach at hand, good for transfers.
Beach, cafes and night markets are very rich.
About 20–40 min walk or a short ride to BIFF Square.

lodging.peak: Busan's summer beach season and the festival (October) tighten rooms and raise prices noticeably. Book several weeks ahead; if booking near a holiday, widen the range to Seoul, Gimhae and other surrounding areas, then take the train or flight.
tips: Want handprint shots: prefer Nampo-dong / Jung-gu, walk to the square at dawn.
Value food & beach: choose Seomyeon / Haeundae, walking and dining at hand.
Before booking, confirm breakfast, parking and EV chargers (drivers especially).
Book ahead in peak season and holidays to avoid no rooms or high prices.

streetFood.title: BIFF Square Street Food – What to Eat & Prices
streetFood.description: Ssiat Hotteok, tteokbokki and more: a guide to BIFF Square street food in Busan — what to eat, typical prices and where the stalls are.
streetFood.h1: BIFF Square Street Food: Ssiat Hotteok & More
streetFood.intro: BIFF Square and the surrounding Nampo-dong food alley are among Busan's best-known street-food spots. The signature is Ssiat Hotteok (씨앗호떡), a seed-and-nut sugar pancake, but the lane is packed with tteokbokki, eomuk (fish cake), gyeran-ppang, twigim and more. Hours vary by vendor — most stalls run from late morning into the evening, with the liveliest scene after sunset.

sections.heading: Ssiat Hotteok — the signature
sections.body: Ssiat Hotteok is a Busan twist on the classic hotteok: a flat fried pancake filled with brown sugar, stuffed with assorted seeds and nuts (ssiat means 'seeds'). It is crisp outside, chewy inside and only mildly sweet — the item most visitors come for.
bullets: Look for long queues at the better-known stalls; turnover keeps them fresh and hot.
Best eaten fresh off the griddle while the filling is still molten.

sections.heading: Other street foods to try
sections.body: The same alley sells the usual Korean street-food line-up, handy for a walking tasting route.
bullets: Tteokbokki (떡볶이) — spicy rice cakes, often with fish cake and noodles.
Eomuk / odeng (어묵) — fish-cake skewers in warm broth, great in cool weather.
Gyeran-ppang (계란빵) — warm egg-in-bread, popular with kids.
Twigim (튀김) — assorted fried seafood and vegetables.

sections.heading: Where the stalls are
sections.body: Stalls cluster along the BIFF Square / Nampo-dong food street and the lanes toward Gukje Market. The square itself is an open corner; the eating happens in the surrounding district a few steps away.

sections.heading: Prices & paying
sections.body: Street food here is cheap and cash-friendly; many stalls prefer cash, though card readers are common.
bullets: Ssiat Hotteok: roughly ₩1,000–₩2,000 each.
Tteokbokki / eomuk: roughly ₩1,000–₩3,000 per portion.
Carry small cash; peak queues move faster with exact change.

faq.q: What is the most famous food at BIFF Square?
faq.a: Ssiat Hotteok (씨앗호떡), the seed-and-nut sugar pancake — the item most travelers come for and the most photographed snack on the street.

faq.q: How much does street food cost?
faq.a: It is inexpensive: a Ssiat Hotteok is roughly ₩1,000–₩2,000, tteokbokki or eomuk about ₩1,000–₩3,000 per portion. Bring small cash for faster queues.

faq.q: Are there vegetarian options?
faq.a: Yes — Ssiat Hotteok, gyeran-ppang and plain eomuk broth are vegetarian-friendly, while tteokbokki and twigim may contain fish sauce or seafood. Ask the vendor if unsure.

faq.q: What are the best hours to eat here?
faq.a: Stalls usually open late morning and run into the evening, with the busiest, liveliest atmosphere after sunset. Weekdays are calmer than festival or weekend nights.

faq.q: Is the food safe to eat?
faq.a: The alley is a long-established, high-turnover food street. Choose busy stalls with steady customers, eat items fresh and hot, and watch the usual street-food hygiene basics.

gettingThere.title: How to Get to BIFF Square (Busan) – Subway, Airport & Parking
gettingThere.description: Directions to BIFF Square in Busan: nearest subway (Jagalchi Station Exit 7), from Busan Station KTX, Gimhae Airport, by bus, taxi and car parking.
gettingThere.h1: How to Get to BIFF Square
gettingThere.intro: BIFF Square sits in Nampo-dong, Jung-gu, Busan, next to Gukje Market and Bosudong Bookstore Street. The closest subway is Jagalchi Station (Busan Line 1), Exit 7, about a 3–5 min walk; Nampo Station (Line 1), Exit 7 is about a 5 min walk as an alternative.

sections.heading: By subway (closest)
sections.body: For most travelers the subway is easiest. Take Busan Line 1 to Jagalchi Station and use Exit 7; follow the district signs about 3–5 min to the square. Nampo Station, Exit 7 is about a 5 min walk if you are already along Line 1.
bullets: From Busan Station: Busan Line 1 to Jagalchi Station, about 15–20 min.
From Seomyeon: Busan Line 1 direct, about 10–15 min.
Use a T-money / transit card for easy transfers.

sections.heading: From Busan Station (KTX)
sections.body: From Seoul, the KTX to Busan Station takes about 2.5 hours. At Busan Station change to Busan Line 1 and ride to Jagalchi Station, then walk about 3–5 min.
bullets: Busan Station → Jagalchi Station: about 15–20 min by subway.
Taxis from Busan Station to BIFF Square take roughly 10–20 min depending on traffic.

sections.heading: From Gimhae Airport
sections.body: Gimhae International Airport (PUS) links to the subway via the Busan–Gimhae Light Rail. Transfer to Busan Line 1 and ride to Jagalchi Station.
bullets: Light Rail to Sasang, then Busan Line 1 toward Jagalchi: about 40–60 min total.
Airport taxis / limousine buses are alternatives if you have heavy luggage.

sections.heading: By bus, taxi and car
sections.body: City and intercity buses stop near Nampo-dong; taxis can drop you at the district edge. Several public and mall parking lots surround the square (Nampo-dong public lot, Gukje Market tower), mostly paid and busy on weekends — arrive early or prefer transit.
bullets: Parking fills fast on peak weekends; transit is strongly recommended.
During the October festival, crowds peak — prefer off-peak visits.

faq.q: What is the nearest station to BIFF Square?
faq.a: Jagalchi Station (Busan Line 1), Exit 7, about a 3–5 min walk. Nampo Station (Line 1), Exit 7 is about a 5 min walk as an alternative.

faq.q: How do I get there from Gimhae Airport?
faq.a: Take the Busan–Gimhae Light Rail and transfer to Busan Line 1 toward Jagalchi Station, about 40–60 min total; taxis and limousine buses are alternatives with luggage.

faq.q: Is there parking, and what does it cost?
faq.a: Several public and mall lots surround the square (Nampo-dong public lot, Gukje Market tower), mostly paid. They fill fast on peak weekends — arrive early or use transit.

faq.q: What is the best way to arrive?
faq.a: For stability and ease, the subway to Jagalchi Station, Exit 7, then a short walk is best. If driving, treat parking and transfer as part of the trip rather than 'park at the door'.

faq.q: Can I walk from Busan Station?
faq.a: It is a long walk; take Busan Line 1 from Busan Station to Jagalchi Station (about 15–20 min) and walk the last few minutes instead.

visitingGuide.title: BIFF Square Visiting Guide – Opening Hours, Best Time & What to See
visitingGuide.description: Plan your BIFF Square visit: the square is open 24 hours (stalls vary), best time to visit, how long to stay, what to see and visitor tips.
visitingGuide.intro: BIFF Square is an open public space next to Gukje Market in Nampo-dong, Jung-gu, Busan. The public square area is open 24 hours year-round, but food stalls and shops keep their own hours — typically late morning to evening, busiest after sunset. There is no gate, ticket or reservation.

sections.heading: Opening hours
sections.body: The public square is open 24 hours and free to enter. Stalls and shops set their own hours and many close late at night or on quiet weekdays — don't expect every stall at dawn or after midnight.
bullets: Public square access: open 24 hours, year-round.
Food stalls & shops: hours vary by vendor (often late morning–evening).

sections.heading: Best time to visit
sections.body: Daytime is good for photos and a relaxed stroll; evening is liveliest for street food and neon. The Busan International Film Festival (usually October) brings the biggest crowds and events.
bullets: Quietest: weekday mornings.
Most atmospheric: after sunset, especially for food.
Busiest: festival period and weekend nights.

sections.heading: How long to stay
sections.body: A relaxed visit is about 1–2 hours, including Star Road and photo stops. Add Gukje Market, Bosudong Bookstreet or Yongdusan Park and it becomes a half-day culture route.

sections.heading: What to see & etiquette
sections.body: Walk Star Road for the director and actor handprints, find the red-carpet marker, and enjoy the Nampo-dong neon. Keep to open paths, respect the handprint plates, and keep late-night noise down.
bullets: Star Road handprints — the square's signature sight.
Red-carpet marker and BIFF marker wall.
Nampo-dong district for food and shopping right next door.

faq.q: What are BIFF Square's opening hours?
faq.a: The public square is open 24 hours, year-round and free. Food stalls and shops keep their own hours and many close late at night or on quiet weekdays.

faq.q: Is BIFF Square free to enter?
faq.a: Yes. It is an open public space with no gate, ticket or reservation — visit any time, and keep late-night noise low out of respect for the neighborhood.

faq.q: How long should I plan for?
faq.a: About 1–2 hours for the square itself; a half day if you add Gukje Market, Bosudong Bookstreet or Yongdusan Park.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit?
faq.a: Weekday mornings are quietest; after sunset is liveliest for food and neon. The October film festival brings the biggest crowds.

faq.q: Can I visit during the Busan International Film Festival?
faq.a: Yes — that is when BIFF Square is most active, with events and crowds. Expect heavy foot traffic and arrive early or off-peak for a calmer look.

handprints.title: BIFF Square Handprints & History – Star Road & the BIFF/PIFF Story
handprints.description: The Star Road handprints at BIFF Square: whose handprints are on the pavement, plus the history of BIFF Square and the Busan International Film Festival.
handprints.intro: Star Road at BIFF Square is paved with the handprints and footprints of over a hundred film directors and actors — one of Busan's most recognizable film landmarks. The square's story is tied to the Busan International Film Festival, founded here in 1996.

sections.heading: The Star Road handprints
sections.body: The pavement holds handprint (and some footprint) plates of Korean and international filmmakers. Among the names are directors such as Hou Hsiao-hsien, Akira Kurosawa and Takeshi Kitano, alongside Korean auteurs — a fan pilgrimage spot embedded in the street.
bullets: Over 100 filmmakers' handprints are set into Star Road.
Plates are embedded in the pavement; crouch low for better photos.
Dawn and dusk light are best and the crowds are thinnest.

sections.heading: History of the square
sections.body: The Busan International Film Festival (then PIFF) was founded in 1996, and this Nampo-dong corner became its birthplace. As the festival's acronym changed from PIFF to BIFF, the area was redeveloped and renamed BIFF Square in 2011 — a Korean film-culture landmark.
bullets: 1996: Busan International Film Festival (PIFF) founded; this corner is its birthplace.
2011: area redeveloped and renamed BIFF Square as PIFF became BIFF.
Today: core stage of 'Community BIFF' and a free public film landmark.

sections.heading: BIFF vs PIFF
sections.body: Both refer to the same festival. 'PIFF' was the original name (Pusan International Film Festival); the city's romanization changed from Pusan to Busan and the festival became BIFF. The square name follows the current BIFF branding.

sections.heading: What to see
sections.body: Beyond the handprints, look for the red-carpet marker and the BIFF marker wall, then link the surrounding market and harbor for the full 'film and city' story.
bullets: Red-carpet marker — the square's most recognizable photo spot.
BIFF marker wall and Nampo-dong neon.
Gukje Market and Bosudong Bookstreet next door.

faq.q: Whose handprints are on Star Road?
faq.a: Over a hundred Korean and international film directors and actors, including names such as Hou Hsiao-hsien, Akira Kurosawa and Takeshi Kitano, alongside Korean auteurs.

faq.q: When was BIFF Square built / renamed?
faq.a: The Busan International Film Festival was founded here in 1996; the area was redeveloped and renamed BIFF Square in 2011 as the festival changed from PIFF to BIFF.

faq.q: What is the difference between BIFF and PIFF?
faq.a: They are the same festival. PIFF was the original name (Pusan International Film Festival); after the city's name changed to Busan, the festival became BIFF. The square follows the current BIFF name.

faq.q: Is it free to see the handprints?
faq.a: Yes. Star Road is an open public space — the handprint plates are free to view any time, day or night.

faq.q: How many handprints are there?
faq.a: Over 100 filmmakers' handprints are set into Star Road, making it one of Busan's most photographed film landmarks.

nearby.title: Things to Do Near BIFF Square – Gukje Market, Jagalchi & More
nearby.description: Near BIFF Square in Busan: Gukje Market, Bosudong Bookstore Street, the 40 Steps, Yongdusan Park & Busan Tower, and Nampo-dong — a half-day culture route.
nearby.h1: Things to Do Near BIFF Square
nearby.intro: BIFF Square is the hub of a walkable Nampo-dong culture cluster. Within a few minutes you can reach Gukje Market, Bosudong Bookstore Street, the 40 Steps, Yongdusan Park and Busan Tower, and Jagalchi Market — easy to string into a half-day route.

sections.heading: Gukje Market (국제시장)
sections.body: A historic market next to BIFF Square, known for food, goods and the 'memory lane' of old Busan. Great to combine with the square for a food-and-history walk.

sections.heading: Bosudong Bookstore Street (보수동 책방골목)
sections.body: A short walk away, this lane of used-bookshops and crafts is a calm, photogenic counterpoint to the busy square — good for gifts and quiet browsing.

sections.heading: 40 Steps (40계단)
sections.body: A modern-history landmark tied to the Korean War refugee era, a few minutes from the square. Simple stairs, but loaded with local memory and signage.

sections.heading: Yongdusan Park & Busan Tower (용두산공원)
sections.body: A hilltop park above Nampo-dong with the Busan Tower and harbor-night views, about a 10–15 min walk. A natural end point for a half-day route.

sections.heading: Nampo-dong & Jagalchi Market
sections.body: Nampo-dong is the shopping-and-food spine around the square; Jagalchi Market, Busan's famous seafood market, is a further walk or short subway hop toward Jagalchi Station.

sections.heading: Sample half-day route
sections.body: Start at BIFF Square (handprints + carpet), cross to Gukje Market for food, wander Bosudong Bookstreet, climb toward Yongdusan Park / Busan Tower for the view, and loop back through Nampo-dong for dinner.
bullets: All on foot except the optional Jagalchi Market leg.
Flat Nampo-dong district — easy with strollers and wheelchairs.
Allow 4–6 hours with food and photos.

faq.q: What is worth visiting near BIFF Square?
faq.a: Gukje Market, Bosudong Bookstore Street, the 40 Steps, Yongdusan Park & Busan Tower, and Nampo-dong — all walkable, plus Jagalchi Market a bit farther.

faq.q: Can I walk everything on foot?
faq.a: Yes. Nampo-dong is flat and the core cluster (BIFF Square, Gukje Market, Bosudong, 40 Steps, Yongdusan) is walkable; Jagalchi Market is a longer walk or a short subway hop.

faq.q: Is it family-friendly?
faq.a: Very. The district is flat and stroller/wheelchair friendly, with food, markets and an easy hilltop park view — good for a relaxed half day.

faq.q: How long for the whole nearby route?
faq.a: About 4–6 hours with food and photos if you include Yongdusan Park and a Nampo-dong dinner.

faq.q: Should I combine it with Jagalchi Market?
faq.a: Only if you like seafood markets — Jagalchi is a further walk or short subway ride from Jagalchi Station, best added as an optional leg.
